key_insight: A large-scale dataset of 200,000+ real researcher interactions reveals diverse query intents and consistent iterative behaviors across a literature-discovery and a scientific QA tool, giving a first empirical lens into how scientists use LLM-powered retrieval-augmented systems in the wild.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of real-world usage data for AI-powered scientific research tools, enabling evidence-based design, evaluation, and safety analysis of LLM-backed research interfaces.
method: Collected and anonymized >200,000 user queries and interaction logs from two deployed tools (literature discovery and scientific question-answering) within an LLM-powered retrieval-augmented generation platform.
Annotated and aggregated interaction metadata (timestamps, clicks, follow-up queries, tool switches, retrieved passages) to enable behavioral analyses while preserving privacy.
Performed descriptive analyses to characterize query intents, session structure, engagement patterns, and differences between the two tool types to surface design and evaluation implications.
impact: Provides a foundational resource for AI/ML practitioners building research-facing LLM systems: enables realistic evaluation, informs UI and retrieval design, and highlights common failure modes and interaction patterns to improve reliability and user trust.
visual_elements: Sankey diagram showing user flows between literature-discovery and QA tools and common next-step transitions
Stacked bar chart of query intent categories (e.g., discovery, clarification, citation lookup) and their relative frequencies
Session timeline heatmap showing distribution of session lengths and points of high follow-up activity
Annotated example interaction (anonymized query → retrieved evidence → LLM answer → follow-up) to illustrate iterative refinement
paper_title: Understanding Usage and Engagement in AI-Powered Scientific Research Tools: The Asta Interaction Dataset
paper_authors: Dany Haddad, Dan Bareket, Joseph Chee Chang, Jay DeYoung, Jena D. Hwang
